drivingQuestion: Does one who remembers mid-Amida that he already prayed stop even in the middle of a blessing?
outcomeNote: The contradiction dissolves once the Shabbat case is distinguished as one where the man is still obligated to pray; Shmuel's ruling stands.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל פּוֹסֵק — וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּאֶמְצַע בְּרָכָה. אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, בְּעַן מִינֵּיהּ: הָנֵי בְּנֵי בֵי רַב דְּטָעוּ וּמַדְכְּרִי דְּחוֹל בְּשַׁבָּת, מַהוּ שֶׁיִּגְמְרוּ? וַאֲמַר לַן: גּוֹמְרִין כׇּל אוֹתָהּ בְּרָכָה?!
segments.en: «And Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said:» One «who was standing in prayer and remembered that he» already «prayed must interrupt» his prayer, «even in the middle of a blessing.» The Gemara challenges this: «Is that so? Didn’t Rav Naḥman say: When we were in the school of Rabba bar Avuh we raised a dilemma before him: Those students in the school of Rav» who «mistakenly recited a» blessing from the «weekday» Amida «on Shabbat, what is» the ruling with regards to «completing» the weekday prayer? «And» Rabba bar Avuh «said to us:» The ruling is that «one must complete that entire blessing.» How then did Rav Yehuda say that one must interrupt his prayer even in the middle of a blessing?

segments.he: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא! הָתָם גַּבְרָא בַּר חִיּוּבָא הוּא, וְרַבָּנַן הוּא דְּלָא אַטְרְחוּהוּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹד שַׁבָּת, אֲבָל הָכָא — הָא צַלִּי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this: «How can you compare» the two cases? «There,» on Shabbat, «the individual is one who is obligated» and should actually recite all eighteen blessings, «and it is the Sages who did not impose upon him in deference to Shabbat» and instituted an abridged formula. «But here, didn’t he» already «pray?» Therefore he can stop, even in the middle of a blessing.
